sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Detailed study guide and resources for Provincial Kingdoms and Resistance by Indian Chiefs are currently being prepared. Check back soon for comprehensive explanations, summary diagrams, and expert preparation recommendations.

Key Dimensions of Study:

  • Definition, scope, and foundational theories.
  • Relevance to General Studies Paper & Contemporary contexts.
  • Core applications and structural framework.

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following founded the independent kingdom of Bengal in the early 18th century?
practiceQuestions.sol: Murshid Quli Khan was appointed as the Dewan of Bengal by Aurangzeb and later became its virtual independent ruler, shifting the capital from Dacca to Murshidabad. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History - Themes in Indian History Part II / Spectrum Modern India]

practiceQuestions.q: The famous city of Jaipur was founded by which of the following Rajput rulers?
practiceQuestions.sol: Sawai Jai Singh II founded the city of Jaipur in 1727 and built astronomical observatories (Jantar Mantar) at Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura, and Varanasi. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval India / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: Who founded the independent state of Awadh (Oudh) in 1722?
practiceQuestions.sol: Saadat Khan, also known as Burhan-ul-Mulk, was appointed governor of Awadh in 1722 and laid the foundation of a strong regional kingdom. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: The independent kingdom of Hyderabad was established in 1724 by whom?
practiceQuestions.sol: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah (Chin Qilich Khan) founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty of Hyderabad in 1724 after defeating Mubariz Khan at the Battle of Shakarkhera. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was the founder of the Sikh Kingdom in Punjab during the early 19th century?
practiceQuestions.sol: Maharaja Ranjit Singh united the various Sikh Misls and established a powerful sovereign state in Punjab with Lahore as its capital. [Primary Reference: NCERT Modern Indian History / Spectrum]

practiceQuestions.q: The Maratha administrative system was headed by a council of ministers known as:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Ashtapradhan was a council of eight ministers that assisted Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in the administration of the Maratha kingdom. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 7/12 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following terms referred to the 25% share of land revenue collected by Marathas from areas outside their direct control?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chauth was a levy amounting to 25% of the land revenue demanded by Marathas to prevent neighboring territories from being plundered, while Sardeshmukhi was an additional 10%. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: Who founded the Jat state of Bharatpur and fortified it in the late 17th and early 18th centuries?
practiceQuestions.sol: While Gokula and Rajaram led early Jat peasant revolts against Aurangzeb, Churaman and Badan Singh laid the foundation of the Bharatpur state, which reached its zenith under Maharaja Suraj Mal. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: The treaty of Purandar was signed in 1665 between Shivaji and which Mughal general?
practiceQuestions.sol: Raja Jai Singh of Amber forced Shivaji to sign the Treaty of Purandar in June 1665, under which Shivaji surrendered 23 of his 35 forts to the Mughals. [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval India / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was the peshwa during the Third Battle of Panipat (1761)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Balaji Baji Rao, popularly known as Nanasaheb, was the Peshwa when the Mar disastrously lost the Third Battle of Panipat against Ahmad Shah Abdali in 1761. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did the 18th-century successor states (such as Bengal, Awadh, and Hyderabad) fail to develop a stable, all-India political structure despite breaking away from the Mughal Empire?
opts: They maintained the flawed centralized agrarian and military structures of the Mughals without addressing fundamental socio-economic issues.
They completely rejected administrative integration with regional chieftains and zamindars.
They focused exclusively on naval trade and neglected territorial consolidation.
They adopted a rigid religious policy that alienated their non-Muslim subjects.
practiceQuestions.sol: The successor states functioned as regional autonomies but retained the core structural flaws of the late Mughal administrative, revenue, and military systems, making them vulnerable to internal corruption and foreign intervention. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the rise of the Maratha confederacy under the Peshwas differ structurally from Shivaji's centralized swarajya model?
opts: Shivaji relied on foreign mercenaries, whereas the Peshwas relied exclusively on local peasantry.

Shivaji's model was a tightly controlled centralized monarchy with direct control over revenue, while the Peshwa period saw the decentralization of power among powerful military chiefs (Scindias, Gaekwads, Holkars, Bhonsles).
The Peshwas abolished the collection of Chauth and Sardeshmukhi in favor of fixed land taxes.
Shivaji focused on northern conquests, while the Peshwas restricted themselves strictly to the Deccan.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Peshwas, the Maratha state transformed from a unified Swarajya into a loose confederacy where military commanders carved out autonomous spheres of influence, leading to internal rivalries. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / NCERT Class 12]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary socio-economic impact of the 'Ijarah' (revenue farming) system introduced in various provincial kingdoms during the 18th century?
opts: It ensured equitable taxation and long-term agricultural prosperity for peasants.
It led to severe peasant exploitation, short-sighted revenue extraction, and the rise of powerful middlemen.
It completely eliminated the role of intermediaries between the state and the cultivator.
It centralized state finances directly under the central monarch.
practiceQuestions.sol: Revenue farming (Ijarah) involved auctioning the right to collect revenue to the highest bidder, who ruthlessly exploited peasants to maximize short-term profits, leading to agrarian distress. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Madhyकालीन Bharat / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the resistance by local chiefs such as the Poligars in South India. What was the core conflict between the Poligars and the British colonial administration?
opts: Religious conversion policies enforced by the East India Company.
Dispute over maritime trade routes in the Indian Ocean.
Disarmament of Poligars, dismantling of their forts, and encroachment on their traditional revenue and military authority.
Introduction of the Ryotwari system which directly benefited the cultivating peasants.
practiceQuestions.sol: The British attempted to dismantle the military and revenue autonomy of the southern Poligars (Palaiyakkarars) by imposing heavy taxes, demanding disarmament, and annexing their forts, sparking fierce resistance (e.g., Kattabomman). [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India / Rajayyan, South Indian Rebellion]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did Haider Ali and Tipu Sultan of Mysore pose a formidable challenge to British expansion in South India compared to other contemporary states?
opts: They relied entirely on traditional feudal levies without modernizing their forces.
They established a centralized modern army trained by Europeans, state-managed trade, and modern administrative reforms.
They avoided foreign alliances and maintained complete isolation from international politics.
They abolished all forms of taxation to gain absolute popular support.
practiceQuestions.sol: Mysore under Haider Ali and Tipu Sultan modernized its military along European lines, introduced state monopolies in trade, built a strong economic base, and pursued progressive administrative reforms. [Primary Reference: NCERT Modern Indian History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the administrative structure of the Sikh Kingdom under Maharaja Ranjit Singh differ from the traditional Mughal or Rajput models?
opts: It was based purely on religious clerical law (Sharia/Sariat equivalent).
It integrated traditional clan affiliations of Misls into a centralized, secularized military state while retaining local revenue collectors (Kardars).
It abolished all standing armies in favor of a decentralized militia.
It operated entirely under the direct supervision of the British East India Company.
practiceQuestions.sol: Ranjit Singh successfully welded the disparate Sikh Misls into a formidable secular military empire, employing European generals (like Allard and Ventura) to train the Fauj-i-Ain while maintaining efficient civil administration through Kardars. [Primary Reference: NCERT Modern Indian History / Khushwant Singh]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the subsidiary alliance system introduced by Lord Wellesley in consolidating British paramountcy over Indian provincial states?
opts: It allowed Indian rulers to maintain independent foreign policies while receiving British financial aid.
It disarmed Indian states, stationed British troops at their expense, exiled their foreign contacts, and reduced them to de facto vassal status.
It encouraged Indian princes to form a united federation against external threats.
It transferred direct administrative control of internal revenues to Indian democratic assemblies.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Subsidiary Alliance effectively stripped Indian states of their military and foreign policy independence, substituting native armies with British garrisons maintained at the host state's expense. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did the Rohilla resistance against the Awadh-British coalition in the late 18th century hold notable geopolitical importance?
opts: It marked the complete expulsion of British influence from northern India.
It exposed how regional successor states like Awadh used British military muscle to expand their territories, paving the way for eventual British paramountcy.
It resulted in the establishment of an independent Rohilla democratic republic.
It was the first instance of a peasant guerrilla war against feudal taxation.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Rohilla War (1773-1774) saw Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh, backed by Warren Hastings' British troops, conquer Rohilkhand, demonstrating how Indian states weakened themselves by depending on the East India Company for regional conquests. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the nature of peasant and tribal resistance (such as the Sannyasi and Fakir uprisings) differ from upper-caste or royal resistance against British expansion in early provincial contexts?
opts: Peasant uprisings were aimed solely at establishing communist rule.

Tribal and peasant resistance stemmed from immediate economic disruptions, dispossession of traditional land rights, and heavy taxation by the new colonial-revenue nexus, rather than merely restoring displaced royalty.
Peasant resistance was exclusively non-violent and relied on legal petitions.
Royal resistance focused on peasant welfare, whereas peasant resistance ignored economic issues.
practiceQuestions.sol: Early resistance by dispossessed peasants, Sannyasis, and Fakirs in Bengal arose directly from the economic exploitation, famine, and revenue extraction unleashed by the Company's dual government and land settlements. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence]

practiceQuestions.q: What structural flaw in the Maratha military-administrative framework contributed most significantly to their defeat against the British in the Anglo-Maratha Wars?
opts: Lack of strategic unity, infighting among Maratha Sardars, financial bankruptcy due to constant plundering without productive economic policies, and inferior diplomacy.
Strict adherence to infantry-only combat without modern artillery.
Rejection of foreign mercenaries and European military advisors.
practiceQuestions.sol: The lack of political cohesion among the Peshwa, Scindia, Holkar, and Bhonsle, coupled with a predatory fiscal model that failed to generate sustainable state revenue, left the Marathas fragmented and vulnerable to British divide-and-rule tactics. [Primary Reference: NCERT Modern Indian History / Spectrum]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the establishment of regional kingdoms in 18th-century India:
1. Murshid Quli Khan stopped sending regular revenue tributes to the Mughal Emperor but continued to acknowledge nominal Mughal suzerainty.
2. Saadat Khan initiated a land revenue settlement in Awadh that reduced the power of powerful regional intermediaries like taluqdars.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Murshid Quli Khan maintained administrative independence in Bengal and remitted regular tributes as a symbolic gesture to keep Delhi pacified without yielding real control. Statement 2 is incorrect: Saadat Khan carried out a fresh assessment of revenues and subdued recalcitrant zamindars, but subsequent rulers and the system often relied heavily on or negotiated with powerful taluqdars rather than systematically eliminating their overarching socio-political dominance in Awadh. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the administrative and military reforms of Tipu Sultan:
1. He introduced a new calendar, a new system of coinage, and restructured the scale of weights and measures.
2. He completely prohibited the employment of French officers in his army to maintain absolute indigenous control.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Tipu Sultan introduced innovative measures including a new luni-solar calendar, new coinage, and standardized weights and measures. Statement 2 is incorrect: Tipu actively sought French assistance, maintained French military advisors, and even planted a 'Tree of Liberty' at Srirangapatna in alliance with French republicans. [Primary Reference: NCERT Modern Indian History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Poligar Rebellions in South India:
1. The Poligars were military chieftains who held administrative and revenue-collecting rights over specific territories under the Nayaka rulers.
2. The rebellion of Veerapandiya Kattabomman against the East India Company took place in the Tirunelveli district.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Poligars (Palaiyakkarars) were feudal lords/military chiefs appointed by the Nayaka rulers of Madurai. Veerapandiya Kattabomman led a fierce resistance against Company tax collection and sovereignty in the Panchalankurichi region of Tirunelveli district during the late 18th century. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India / Rajayyan]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Anglo-Maratha Wars:
1. The Treaty of Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War and brought about a period of relative peace between the Marathas and the British for nearly two decades.
2. The Second Anglo-Maratha War resulted in the Peshwa signing the Subsidiary Alliance through the Treaty of Bassein (1802).
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Treaty of Salbai concluded the First Anglo-Maratha War, securing 20 years of peace. Following internal strife, Peshwa Baji Rao II signed the subsidiary Treaty of Bassein in 1802, triggering the Second Anglo-Maratha War. [Primary Reference: NCERT Modern Indian History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber:
1. He established capital at Jaipur and constructed advanced astronomical instruments in masonry.
2. He strictly prohibited scientific exchanges with European astronomers and mathematicians.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Sawai Jai Singh II founded Jaipur and built masonry observatories (Jantar Mantar). Statement 2 is incorrect: He was deeply interested in European science, mathematics, and astronomy, studying texts such as Euclid's geometry and works of De La Hire, and even sending envoys to Portugal. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / NCERT]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the resistance of Kerala Varma Pazhassi Raja:
1. Pazhassi Raja led the Kottayam resistance against the British East India Company in Malabar.
2. He utilized guerrilla warfare tactics in the dense forests of Wayanad against colonial forces.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Pazhassi Raja (the 'Lion of Kerala') organized heroic resistance against Company rule in Kottayam (Malabar) over revenue collection rights and British high-handedness, employing effective guerrilla warfare in the Wayanad hills. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India / A. Sreedhara Menon]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the administrative innovations of Maratha rule under Shivaji:
1. Shivaji completely abolished the traditional hereditary village headman system (Patil and Kulkarni).
2. The revenue assessment under Shivaji was based on careful measurement of land and accounted for a fixed share of the produce.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Shivaji did not abolish hereditary village officers like Patils and Kulkarnis; rather, he exercised strict central supervision over them to curb their oppression of peasants. Statement 2 is correct: Influenced by Malik Amber's revenue system, Shivaji instituted systematic land surveys and fixed the state's share (initially 33%, later increased to 40%). [Primary Reference: NCERT Medieval India / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Hyderabadi state founded by Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah:
1. It acted as an absolute buffer state and completely isolated itself from the Carnatic wars and Maratha incursions.
2. Asaf Jah maintained religious tolerance and appointed Hindus to high administrative and financial positions.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Hyderabad was deeply embroiled in Carnatic politics, imperial intrigues, and frequent military conflicts with the Marathas (e.g., Battle of Palkhed). Statement 2 is correct: Asaf Jah pursued a tolerant administrative policy, appointing Hindu officials like Puran Chand to key financial and administrative posts. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the resistance led by Velu Nachiyar and Dheeran Chinnamalai:
1. Velu Nachiyar was the queen of Sivaganga who fought the British with the military assistance of Hyderabadi and Mysorean troops.
2. Dheeran Chinnamalai led the Kongu Vellalar resistance against the British in the Kongu region of Tamil Nadu.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Velu Nachiyar (Veeramangai) allied with Hyderabadi/Mysore forces (securing troops from Tipu/Haider) to recapture Sivaganga. Dheeran Chinnamalai organized the Kongu regional resistance, utilizing guerrilla tactics against the British East India Company. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern India / State Board History Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 18th-century economic and social conditions in provincial kingdoms:
1. Despite political decentralization and constant warfare, regional trade routes flourished as merchants sought safer corridors away from imperial Delhi.
2. The monetization of the rural economy increased, making cash-crop production and revenue demands more stringent on the peasantry.
Which of the statements given below is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. While imperial decline disrupted central stability, regional capitals like Hyderabad, Lucknow, Jaipur, and Murshidabad fostered vibrant local economies, vibrant internal trade, and heightened monetization of rural output to satisfy cash-based revenue demands. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / NCERT Class 12 History]
